## What session 7 is for {.scrollable}
::::: columns

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The mathematics

- Choose which of the course's models fits a new outcome — a number, a yes/no, ordered or unordered categories
- Read every result as a sentence, in units, and say what it does **not** license
- Compare OLS with ridge, the lasso and the elastic net on data the models did not see

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The Python

- Load a paper's data file — `.dta`, `.csv` — into pandas
- Run the code cells of sessions 3 to 5 on new data, changing only the variable names
- Run a whole analysis as one script in VS Codium, step by step

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The international business

- Use international-business data from published papers
- Explain a result to someone who will not read the code
- Keep a log a referee could follow

::::

:::::

## What to do, and how long it takes {.center .scrollable}

## Thirty minutes {.scrollable}

The workshop is three hours at your own keyboard, in a folder of your own. It goes well if that
folder is ready when you arrive, and badly if you spend the first hour installing.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Re-read the four abstracts: the question, and what the data are | 10 min |
| **2** | Set up your session-07 folder: Python, four packages, the scripts | 15 min |
| **3** | Write two lines per paper, from memory | 5 min |

::: {.muted}
Everything on these slides is also on the pre-session page, `07-replication-workshop/00-pre-session/README.md`,
where the commands can be copied.
:::

## Re-read the papers {.center .scrollable}

## The four papers, and the models you will fit {.scrollable}

| # | Paper | What you will fit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fraiberger, Lee, Puy & Ranciere (2021), *Media sentiment and international asset prices* | OLS, binary, ordinal and multinomial logits |
| 2 | Saganowski, Bródka, Koziarski & Kazienko (2019), *Analysis of group evolution prediction …* | binary, ordinal and multinomial logits |
| 3 | Blonigen & Piger (2014), *Determinants of foreign direct investment* | OLS, ridge, lasso, elastic net |
| 4 | Topalova & Khandelwal (2011), *Trade liberalization and firm productivity* | OLS, binary, ordinal and multinomial logits, ridge, lasso, elastic net |

::: {.step}
You read these before sessions 2 to 6. Re-read the **abstract** and the description of the
**data**: what one observation is, and what is measured.
:::

## Set up your folder {.center .scrollable}

## A folder of your own, not the repository {.scrollable}

Make an empty folder — `Desktop/session-07` — and open it in VS Codium (**File → Open Folder…**).
In its terminal: plain Python, four packages by name, the scripts, the check.

::::: panel-tabset
### macOS

```bash
open /Applications/Python\ 3*/Install\ Certificates.command   # python.org Python only, once
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install pandas statsmodels scikit-learn matplotlib
curl -LO https://warint.github.io/quantitative-methods/session-07-scripts.zip
unzip session-07-scripts.zip
python check_setup.py
```

### Linux

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install pandas statsmodels scikit-learn matplotlib
curl -LO https://warint.github.io/quantitative-methods/session-07-scripts.zip
unzip session-07-scripts.zip
python check_setup.py
```

No `unzip`? `sudo apt install unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu) or `sudo dnf install unzip` (Fedora).

### Windows

```powershell
py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install pandas statsmodels scikit-learn matplotlib
$zip = "https://warint.github.io/quantitative-methods/session-07-scripts.zip"
Invoke-WebRequest $zip -OutFile session-07-scripts.zip
Expand-Archive session-07-scripts.zip -DestinationPath .
python check_setup.py
```
:::::

::: {.muted}
No `requirements.txt`, nothing to download from Dataverse: each script reads its paper's data
from the course site. Every line of the check should say `OK`.
:::
